chunks: Jābir ibn Ismāʿīl narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام:
That a man asked ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام about standing in prayer during the night with recitation, so he said to him: “Receive glad tidings.
Whoever prays a tenth of the night for Allah, sincerely seeking the reward of Allah, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels:
“Write for this servant of Mine, among the good deeds, the number of what grows in the night of seed, leaf, and tree, and the number of every stalk, frond, and pasture.”

Whoever prays a ninth of the night, Allah grants him ten answered supplications and gives him his book in his right hand. Whoever prays an eighth of the night, Allah grants him the reward of a patient martyr, sincere in intention, and he is granted intercession regarding his household. Whoever prays a seventh of the night rises from his grave on the day he is resurrected with his face like the moon on the night of fullness, until he passes over the Sirat with the secure ones. Whoever prays a sixth of the night is recorded among the oft-returning ones, and what has preceded of his sin is forgiven for him. Whoever prays a fifth of the night contends alongside Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of the All-Merciful, in his dome. Whoever prays a quarter of the night is among the first of the successful, until he passes over the Sirat like a violent wind and enters Paradise without reckoning. Whoever prays a third of the night, no angel remains except that he envies him for his rank with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is said to him: Enter from whichever of the eight gates of Paradise you wish. Whoever prays half a night, even if he were given the fill of the earth in gold seventy thousand times, it would not equal his reward; and by that, for him with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is better than seventy slaves he frees from the descendants of Ismāʿīl. Whoever prays two-thirds of a night, he shall have of good deeds the measure of the sand of ʿĀlij, the least of which is a good deed heavier than Mount Uḥud ten times.

Whoever prays a complete night, reciting the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and remembering, is given of reward such that at the very least he comes out from sins as his mother gave birth to him. There are written for him, of good deeds, the number of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created, and the like of them in degrees. Light is established in his grave, sin and envy are removed from his heart, he is granted protection from the punishment of the grave, he is given immunity from the Fire, and he is resurrected among the secure. And the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels:

“O My angels, look at My servant: he kept a night alive seeking My pleasure. Settle him in al-Firdaws, and for him therein are one hundred thousand cities; in every city is all that souls desire and eyes delight in, and what has not occurred to any mind besides what I have prepared for him of honor, increase, and nearness.”

key_terms.الصِّرَاطِ: the bridge crossed in the afterlife
key_terms.الْأَوَّابِينَ: those who repeatedly return to Allah in repentance and devotion
key_terms.قِيَامِ اللَّيْلِ: standing in worship during the night
key_terms.مَرْضَاتِي: My pleasure, meaning Allah’s good pleasure

ai.seo_question: What rewards are mentioned in hadith for praying during the night and performing Qiyām al-Layl?
ai.summary: This hadith extols Qiyām al-Layl and describes ascending degrees of reward according to how much of the night is spent in salat, recitation, dhikr, ruku', and sajdah. It emphasizes sincerity, divine reward, answered du'a, forgiveness, safety in the afterlife, and nearness to Allah through devoted night worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1374 - Jabir ibn Isma'il narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (as), that a man asked Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) about praying during the night with recitation.

Whoever prays a tenth of the night for the sake of Allah (swt) with sincerity, seeking His reward, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, will say to His angels: 'Write for My servant the good deeds equal to every seed, leaf, and tree that grows in the night, and the number of every stalk, frond, and pasture.'
Whoever prays a ninth of the night, Allah (swt) grants him ten answered supplications and gives him his book (record) in his right hand.

Whoever prays an eighth of the night, Allah (swt) grants him the reward of a patient martyr with sincere intention, and he will intercede for his family.
Whoever prays a seventh of the night will rise from his grave on the Day of Resurrection with a face as bright as the full moon and cross the Sirat (bridge) with the secure ones.
Whoever prays a sixth of the night is counted among the Awabin (those who frequently turn to Allah (swt) in repentance), and their past sins are forgiven.
Whoever prays a fifth of the night will be beside Ibrahim (as), the Friend of the Merciful, in his dome.
Whoever prays a fourth of the night will be among the first to succeed and cross the Sirat like a fierce wind, entering Paradise without reckoning.
Whoever prays a third of the night will have all the angels envy his rank with Allah (swt) and be told, 'Enter any of the eight gates of Paradise you wish.'
Whoever prays half the night would not find the equivalent of his reward even if given the earth's fill in gold seventy thousand times, and it would be better than freeing seventy slaves from the descendants of Isma'il (Ishmael).
Whoever prays two-thirds of the night will have good deeds equivalent to the grains of sand in Alij [a desert area that has a lot of sand], and even the least of them is heavier than Mount Uhud ten times.

Whoever prays an entire night reciting the Book of Allah (swt), bowing, prostrating, and remembering Him will be given such a reward that he emerges from his sins like the day he was born, with good deeds equal to all that Allah (swt) has created and the same in degrees. Light will be established in his grave, envy and sin will be removed from his heart, he will be protected from the punishment of the grave, and he will be granted freedom from the Fire. He will be resurrected among the secure, and Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, will say to His angels:

'Look at My servant who spent his night seeking My pleasure. Make him dwell in Firdaws (the highest part of Paradise), where he will have one hundred thousand cities, each containing all that souls desire and eyes delight in and more, beyond what has ever crossed the heart of anyone, prepared for him as an honor and increase and closeness to Me.'
